answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit a claim; randomly selected peers audit claims against signed task receipts, and a proven lie burns the stake while rewarding the auditors. A juniper registry can record each lock and penalty, while a forge checks receipts and a mirror view lets agents compare outcomes. Creating many identities then multiplies the capital tied up and the risk of forfeiture, so a sybil attacker must spend real resources rather than merely mint names.
